## * between INTERVAL and INT64 values
# Sources: BigQuery's operators reference (interval arithmetic operators); GoogleSQL's
# compliance/functions_testlib_interval.cc (interval multiply); BigQuery answers.

SELECT INTERVAL '1:2:3' HOUR TO SECOND * 10
=> "0-0 0 10:20:30"

SELECT INTERVAL 35 SECOND * 4
=> "0-0 0 0:2:20"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 YEAR * 0
=> "0-0 0 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 YEAR * -9999
=> "-9999-0 0 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 MONTH * 1007
=> "83-11 0 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 DAY * -11
=> "0-0 -11 0:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 HOUR * 9999
=> "0-0 0 9999:0:0"

SELECT INTERVAL 1 MICROSECOND * -3
=> "0-0 0 -0:0:0.000003"

# Months, days and time multiply apart, without carrying into each other.
SELECT MAKE_INTERVAL(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) * 11
=> "0-11 22 33:44:55"

SELECT MAKE_INTERVAL(0, -1, -2, -3, -4, -5) * -3
=> "0-3 6 9:12:15"

SELECT CAST(NULL AS INTERVAL) * 1
=> null

SELECT INTERVAL 1 YEAR * CAST(NULL AS INT64)
=> null

# BigQuery also takes INT64 * INTERVAL, which its operators reference does not list. Source:
# BigQuery answers.
SELECT 3 * INTERVAL 2 DAY
=> "0-0 6 0:0:0"

SELECT CAST(NULL AS INT64) * INTERVAL 1 DAY
=> null

SELECT INTERVAL 2 YEAR * 10000
=> error: Interval field months '240000' is out of range -120000 to 120000

SELECT INTERVAL 3660000 DAY * -2
=> error:

SELECT INTERVAL 999999 DAY * 99999999999
=> error: Interval field days '99999899999000001' is out of range -3660000 to 3660000
